prompts: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, using a wide overhead composition to fully frame the cloud platform. Thin mist floats in the foreground, the midground features a jade-brick cloud terrace, and the background shows a waterfall and layered mountain peaks with low-resolution pixel edges subtly flickering. Twelve teacups gather from all sides into a neat square formation. Their glazed bodies reflect cold daylight, limbs gently swaying in preparation. The camera slowly descends in an overhead tracking move, emphasizing the relationship between the platform and formation.
As feet land, pixel dust on the cloud surface slightly lifts, and cold mist trails backward behind them. The steady camera pan reinforces uniformity.

Shot 3 cuts sharply to a close-up, focusing closely on the rim, handle, and hand of a lead teacup. Occasional mist threads drift across the foreground, while the background formation blurs into blue-white pulsating blocks. The handle-hand and other hand clap in sync, producing a sharp cold highlight on the ceramic surface at impact.

Shot 4 cuts directly to a wide eye-level pull-back, showing the entire group dispersing from a square into a lotus formation. Platform patterns and railing lines naturally guide the viewer’s gaze toward the center. The central teacup leads slightly ahead, guiding the outer circle to spiral outward. Under cool diffuse light, the twelve cups resemble jade petals unfurling, limbs extending at consistent angles, the transition smooth. Background waterfall The camera pulls back with slight orbiting, emphasizing the pattern’s emergence.

Shot 5 cuts to a low-angle wide shot from beneath the edge of the jade bridge. Foreground includes railings and passing mist, background features a high waterfall cascading down. Teacups leap onto the bridge one by one, completing synchronized spins. Three distinct phases—kicking off, lifting body, landing—are clearly visible. As feet leave the ground, mist splits into arcs. Backlight outlines the rims in silver. Wind The camera rises upward, following motion, creating a sense of elevation.

Shot 6 cuts sharply to a medium-close eye-level shot focused on the bridge surface. The composition uses longitudinal brick textures to create a sense of speed. Several teacups slide past the lens, others maintain same-speed movement behind. Arms remain extended for balance, bodies slightly leaning forward. The camera moves laterally opposite the direction of travel, emphasizing horizontal flow.

Shot 7 transitions via a soft misty dissolve to a close-up eye-level shot moving through peach blossom mist. Foreground features blurred pink-white pixel petals. Focus locks on a middle row of teacups advancing with arm swings. A faint peach hue accents the cool palette without disrupting it. Arms sweep outward from chest, leg steps tightly timed. Mist swirls in response to motion. Wind becomes more intimate, near ear level. The camera steadily pushes through the mist, creating a sense of entering the performance core.

Shot 8 cuts sharply to a wide overhead view. The lotus pond walkway unfolds in geometric zigzags. A corner of a lotus leaf appears in the foreground, cloud platform and bridge visible in the background, evoking spatial memory. Twelve teacups split into two columns, crossing paths while maintaining equal distance. Limb motions shift from wide swings to compact steps. Body turns and foot crossings are clearly distinguishable. Cold water below reflects fragmented light. The camera slowly pans overhead, fully mapping the crossing path.

Shot 9 cuts sharply to a medium eye-level shot facing the side of the walkway. A full row of teacups performs synchronized kicks. Foreground and background layers are distinct. Lift, extend, and land actions are highly synchronized. Droplets separate into pixelated particles mid-air before falling. Ceramic highlights and droplet reflections flash in sync. The camera slightly follows with a lateral pan, emphasizing continuous bursts.

Shot 10 cuts sharply to a far-medium low-angle shot on an open platform before the waterfall. Strong backlight makes the mist glow white and bright. Twelve teacups spin in unison—outer ring counterclockwise, inner clockwise—forming dual-layer melodies. Limbs extend then retract. As bodies rotate, rim light circles form arcs. The waterfall behind creates a high-contrast dynamic backdrop. The camera orbits slightly while pulling back, making the rotation structure clear.

Shot 11 cuts sharply to a close-up, focusing on the tea surface inside a single cup. The rim frames the edge of the image naturally. Background reduces to blurred waterfall highlights. The surface trembles finely due to recent collective rotation, ripples spreading outward from the center. Cold light glides across the liquid surface. Occasionally, tiny droplets rise and fall back.

Shot 12 connects via a brief fade-in/fade-out to a medium eye-level shot returning to the cloud platform. Low-lying mist in the foreground, layered mountains in the background. Twelve teacups re-form and perform wave-like swaying. Motion passes left to right—first arms, then body tilt, finally light foot taps completing the cycle. Wind regains dominance. The camera slowly moves horizontally opposite the wave direction, enhancing the propagation effect.

Shot 13 cuts hard from the previous shot to a high-angle wide shot, with the cloud platform's paving stones and bridge corridors forming geometric converging lines. Twelve teacups begin moving in a figure-eight pattern, with the left and right groups meeting at the center before diverging. The route is clear, spacing remains consistent, and there are no collisions. Arm swing amplitude decreases while foot frequency increases. The camera performs a slight diving push from above, emphasizing the path pattern.

Shot 14 cuts hard from the previous shot to a close-up eye-level view, focusing on several front-row teacups, with background performers forming an orderly blurred layer. All teacups simultaneously retract their arms and squat down, drawing arms from the sides to the chest, knees bending, bodies lowering, and gazes fixed forward, forming a distinct ending posture. Cold mist is compressed downward, creating a low-lying wave of air as it sinks. Highlights on the porcelain shrink to the rim and shoulders. The camera gently lowers to match the motion, completing the final gesture.

Shot 15 transitions softly from the previous shot via fade, ending in a wide eye-level static frame centered on the cloud platform. All teacups spread out into a standard circular formation. Thin mist slowly drifts into the foreground, while the background waterfall and clouds maintain steady flow. A blank space remains at the center of the formation, resembling a cold jade imprint. The twelve teacups slightly lift their heads after holding the final pose, limbs still but wisps of fog like fabric edges and residual ripples inside the cups continue to move. Overall cool ambient lighting remains consistent. Wind continues as a lingering tail The camera slowly pulls back and holds, allowing the circular formation to leave a crisp, orderly finale within a pixelated fantasy realm.
